SMEA.L.evidence_2025_10_24: 2026-09-16 REFRESH ADDITION. The refreshed common calendar recovered 2025-10-24 (a Friday the previous build's panel did not carry -- VWRP.L has no own bar for it, so it entered via the ^FTSE infill; see CONFIG['calendar_note']). On that date SMEA.L's raw Yahoo bar is Open=High=Low=Close=9099.12 with Volume=0 against 7889 on 2025-10-23 and 7973 on 2025-10-27 -- a +14.71% jump given straight back (-12.32%) the next session. Same signature as the DBMG.L placeholders below: a flat OHLC, zero-volume print. No MSCI Europe index moved 14.7% that day, and the broad equity lines (VWRP.L, ISF.L) are forward-filled flat on it. Left in the panel it inflated SMEA.L's 5y vol from 14.03% to 16.64% and its skew from -0.107 to +0.891. The single bar is masked (no price invented); the 2025-10-23 -> 2025-10-27 return is dropped, not synthesised. A panel-wide scan for the same signature (flat OHLC + zero volume + an >8% move reversed >8% the next session, on feeds where flat/zero-volume bars are not the norm) finds exactly two instances in the whole 10y window: this one and WLDS.L.
SMEA.L.evidence: Yahoo's SMEA.L feed is quoted in GBP (pounds) up to 2023-11-24 and in GBp (pence) from 2024-04-25, with a stretch in between carried on the EUR line: the 2023-11-27 bar is exactly 100x the prior scale PLUS 14.60%, and the 2024-04-25 bar gives that 14.60% straight back (-14.58%); 1.1460 x 0.8542 = 0.979. The 100x step is corrected by the segment rescale; the two residual 14.6% jumps are quote-line artefacts, so the whole mis-quoted stretch (most of which Yahoo has no data for at all) is masked. The surviving 2023-11-24 -> 2024-04-25 level move of +9.1% is a genuine five-month MSCI Europe return and the level series stays continuous.

config.calendar_note: The refreshed common calendar gained TWO trading days inside the OLD window -- 2025-10-24 and 2026-03-06 -- and dropped none. fetch_data.py builds the calendar as VWRP.L's own trading days UNIONED with the ^FTAS/^FTSE trading days that VWRP.L is missing inside its own operating range. That union rule is what SPEC section 7 requires in order to carry the 2026-09-16 bar at all (VWRP.L's Yahoo series stops on 2026-09-15), but it is WIDER than SPEC section 7's literal wording ('the union of VWRP.L days plus the one patched date 2026-09-16'): it also recovers any other day VWRP.L's EOD-NAV feed skipped. Two such days exist in the 10y window and both are genuine LSE sessions (Fridays; individual LSE equities, the FX pairs and ^FTSE all have bars; 68 and 73 of the 84 panel columns move on them). Recovering them is an improvement on the previous build, which silently dropped them -- but it, not the window roll, is the whole of the 1259 -> 1261 change in return days, and on both dates the BENCHMARK column is a forward-fill, so those two regression observations pair a manufactured 0.00% benchmark return with each asset's real return. That pairing is exactly what made the two bad prints above damaging. fetch_log.json records the calendar change under tickers.CALENDAR.issues. SPEC section 7's wording should be amended to match the union rule the pipeline actually implements.

definitions._scope: Every statistic below is computed on GBP total-return indices (split-adjusted price plus reinvested dividends, rebuilt by fetch_data.py; Yahoo's Adj Close is discarded). Daily statistics are annualised with 252 trading days.
definitions.mean_ann_arith: Arithmetic mean of daily returns x 252. The correct input to a mean-variance optimiser (it is the expectation of the one-period return).
definitions.cagr: (Level_end / Level_start)^(365.25 / days) - 1. Geometric, lower than the arithmetic mean by roughly half the variance. For a series built from RETURNS (the sleeve index, every portfolio's realised and backtest series) the level is based at 100 on the trading day BEFORE the first return -- published as level_base_date next to the statistic -- so total_return compounds every return in the series and cagr is the annualisation of exactly that total return. Builds before 2026-09-17 based that level ON the first return date, which dropped the first period's return from total_return and cagr while keeping it in every other statistic; corrected here after a blind verification (moonshot sleeve total return 52.85% -> 54.76%).
definitions.total_return: Level_end / Level_base - 1 = prod(1 + r_t) - 1 over the whole series.
definitions.level_base_date: Date the level series is based at 100: the panel observation immediately before the first return.
definitions.first_period_return: The series' first return (the one the pre-2026-09-17 level base dropped from total_return and cagr); published so any earlier figure can be restated as (1 + old) x (1 + first_period_return) - 1.
definitions.vol_ann: Sample standard deviation of daily returns (ddof = 1) x sqrt(252).
definitions.sharpe: (mean_ann_arith - rf) / vol_ann, rf = BoE Bank Rate 0.0375.
definitions.downside_dev_ann: sqrt( mean( min(r_t - rf_daily, 0)^2 ) ) x sqrt(252). The mean is taken over ALL observations, not only the losing ones.
definitions.skew: Sample skewness of daily returns, bias-corrected (scipy, bias=False).
definitions.max_drawdown: min( Level_t / cummax(Level)_t - 1 ) with the peak and trough dates.
definitions.var95_daily / var99_daily: Historical Value at Risk: the negative of the 5th (1st) percentile of the daily return sample, reported as a positive loss.
definitions.cvar95_daily / cvar99_daily: Historical Conditional VaR / expected shortfall: the negative of the mean of all returns at or below the VaR cut-off.
definitions.beta_vwrp / beta_ftas: OLS slope of the asset's EXCESS daily return on the benchmark's excess daily return; alpha is the intercept x 252; R2 the regression R-squared. Benchmarks: VWRP.L (FTSE All-World in GBP) and ^FTAS (FTSE All-Share).
definitions.beta_up: OLS slope computed only on the days when the benchmark's EXCESS return was > 0.
definitions.beta_down: OLS slope computed only on the days when the benchmark's excess return was < 0.
definitions.beta_asymmetry: beta_up - beta_down. Positive = participates more on the way up than on the way down, i.e. a positively skewed payoff against the market.
definitions.portfolio_beta_convention: PORTFOLIO beta / beta+ / beta- / beta_ftas are the weighted sums of the constituent betas over ALL 37 core lines with the weights summing to 1 -- the betas of the sleeve AS HELD, including the 2.5% SPCX policy weight. Beta is linear in the weights, so this is the arithmetically correct figure for the holding. Because SPCX's betas come from only 67 daily bars (beta 2.95, beta+ 8.34, beta- 1.40) they are not estimates, and that 2.5% line moves the portfolio beta+ by about 0.21. The *_excl_spcx fields give the same statistics for the optimised 97.5% alone, renormalised to 1; the first release reported only those, unlabelled.
definitions.52_week_high_low: Trailing 365 calendar days to the as-of date, from the INTRADAY High / Low columns of data/raw (split-adjusted to the as-of convention; GBp lines /100; GBP versions at the as-of FX rate). pct_below_52w_high = price_local / high_52w_local - 1 is computed from that SAME high, so the two agree. The close-only high/low and the close-basis percentage are reported alongside as high_52w_close_local / pct_below_52w_high_close_basis; f52_basis records which basis each row actually used.
definitions.valuation_multiples: trailing_pe, forward_pe, price_to_book and ev_to_ebitda are priced at the 2026-09-16 close, not at yfinance's live 2026-09-17 .info quote: each Yahoo multiple is rescaled by close(as-of)/price-at-fetch (both in Yahoo's own units), which reproduces price/EPS exactly. The unscaled Yahoo values are kept as *_yahoo_live.
definitions.market_cap: market_cap = market_cap_gbp = shares outstanding x GBP price per share at the 2026-09-16 close. Yahoo's info['marketCap'] is in the company's OWN reporting currency (USD, HKD, AUD, EUR ...) and is priced live; it is kept as market_cap_yahoo_raw_local_ccy. market_cap_usd_m converts the GBP figure at the as-of GBPUSD rate. enterprise_value_gbp = market_cap_gbp + (total debt - total cash) converted to GBP, own-calculated.
definitions.optimiser_global_search: Each non-convex objective (max Sharpe, max Sortino, max return at target vol) is solved by SLSQP from 96 random feasible starts plus every other solved portfolio as a start, repeated for up to 4 cross-seeding rounds, and is then checked against every other feasible portfolio in the set on its own objective (the run aborts if any is dominated). The 0.5% pairwise-transfer probe reported separately establishes LOCAL optimality only.
definitions.upside_capture_monthly / downside_captur: Mean monthly excess return of the asset divided by the mean monthly excess return of the benchmark, over up months / down months.
definitions.covariance_sample: Pandas sample covariance of daily returns (ddof = 1) x 252, on the complete-case matrix of the optimiser universe.
definitions.covariance_ledoit_wolf: Ledoit & Wolf (2004) constant-correlation shrinkage. Sigma = delta*F + (1-delta)*S, where S is the MLE sample covariance (1/T), F_ij = r_bar * sigma_i * sigma_j with r_bar the average sample correlation (F_ii = S_ii), and delta = max(0, min(1, ((pi - rho)/gamma)/T)). pi = sum_ij (1/T) sum_t (x_ti x_tj - s_ij)^2 ; rho = sum_i pi_ii + sum_{i!=j} (r_bar/2)[sqrt(s_jj/s_ii) theta_ii,ij + sqrt(s_ii/s_jj) theta_jj,ij] with theta_ii,ij = (1/T) sum_t (x_ti^2 - s_ii)(x_ti x_tj - s_ij) ; gamma = sum_ij (f_ij - s_ij)^2. Annualised x 252.
definitions.expected_return_capm_or_yield: rf + beta_own x ERP for equities, equity ETFs, commodity ETCs and the trend fund; redemption yield for the two individual gilts; distribution yield minus a 1% expected default loss for the high-yield and EM credit ETFs; US 10y plus the GBP-USD policy-rate differential for IBTM.L (accumulating, GBP-hedged US Treasury 20y+).
definitions.expected_return_blend: 0.5 x historical + 0.5 x CAPM/yield. The optimiser input. Sample means are the noisiest input to mean-variance optimisation (Michaud 1989); an equal blend with a structural estimate halves the weight on that noise.
definitions.portfolio_weights: Fractions of the GBP 160,000 core sleeve. SPCX carries a fixed policy weight of 2.5% (SPEC section 5) and is outside the covariance matrix; the optimiser allocates the remaining 97.5%.
definitions.ex_ante_vol_lw_optimiser_part: sqrt(w' Sigma_LW w) with w summing to 0.975. This is the quantity the 12% 'moderate risk' constraint binds on: it treats the 2.5% SPCX policy weight as contributing no variance, because SPCX has only 65 daily bars and is excluded from the optimiser covariance.
definitions.ex_ante_vol_full_core_incl_spcx: sqrt(w' Sigma_core w) over all 37 core lines with w summing to 1, using a pairwise-complete daily sample covariance (SPCX's row and column come from its 65 overlapping bars and are NOT reliable), repaired to the nearest PSD matrix by eigenvalue clipping.
definitions.marginal_risk_contribution: MCR_i = (Sigma w)_i / sigma_p ; RC_i = w_i x MCR_i ; sum_i RC_i = sigma_p exactly (Euler decomposition).
definitions.backtest: Fixed target weights rebalanced at every month end on month-end GBP total-return levels, so each month's portfolio return is the weighted average of the constituents' monthly returns. No transaction costs, taxes, spreads or FX charges.
definitions.unicorn_sleeve_index: Equal-weight, daily-rebalanced across the names with data on each date, starting from the first date on which at least 20 of the 40 are live.
definitions.combined_portfolio: 80% headline core + 20% unicorn sleeve, GBP 200,000 in total.
definitions.wacc: WACC = E/(D+E) x Ke + D/(D+E) x Kd x (1 - t), with E = market capitalisation, D = total debt, Ke = rf + beta_own x ERP, Kd = interest expense (FY) / total debt bounded to 0-30% (fallback rf + 2% where interest expense or debt is missing), t = income tax expense / pretax income bounded to 0-35% (fallback 25% where pretax income is missing or negative). Every raw input is kept in the same row so the Excel model can recompute the derived figures with live formulas.
definitions.shares: floor(GBP allocated / GBP price per unit) at the 2026-09-16 close. The two individual gilts are priced at their clean price per GBP 100 nominal.

IPWR.name: Ideal Power Inc.
IPWR.thesis: Ideal Power licenses B-TRAN, the only bidirectional bipolar transistor in existence: one device that conducts and blocks in both directions, halving conduction loss versus the back-to-back MOSFET/IGBT pairs every solid-state circuit breaker uses today. Nvidia's 800VDC Rubin Ultra rack architecture creates a socket that no incumbent device fills well, and a US hyperscaler is co-developing an 800V DC prototype for exactly that architecture. Market cap $63.9m at the 2026-09-16 close with $41.3m of cash and essentially no debt, so the market values the whole platform at roughly $22m.
IPWR.why_10x: 10x = $639m; since $41m of the $64m is cash, the operating business need only reach ~$598m. That requires one pathway - datacentre SSCB or EV contactor - to convert into a production design-in with device or royalty revenue in the tens of millions. An emerging power-semi platform with a named hyperscaler and a named auto OEM at $600m is unremarkable for the category. 100x = $6.4bn is arithmetically live (Navitas has traded near that on GaN) if B-TRAN becomes standard content in both DC datacentre protection and EV contactors; low probability, but the ~14-15 quarter runway is long enough to find out.
IPWR.what_kills_it: Pre-revenue for over a decade with a prior pivot (it was a solar inverter company) and $5,800 of quarterly revenue; hyperscaler co-development routinely ends without a purchase order and the partner is unnamed so nothing can be independently verified; Infineon/onsemi/Wolfspeed/Navitas can attack the same sockets with proven SiC and GaN at scale, and double-sided wafer processing is a real yield risk at volume.

At US$37.3m it is the cheapest position in the sleeve in absolute dollars, with A$10.3m of cash at March 2026 and no debt. On 2026-06-30 it signed a three-year Quantum Compute Agreement with IonQ - but note the direction of the money: Archer PAYS IonQ US$1.5m over three years for Forte/Tempo-class access and reselling rights, so this is commercial intent, not a backer.
AXE.AX.why_10x: 10x = ~US$373m (A$525m), reachable by either of two independent routes. Quantum route: a working room-temperature spin readout at wafer scale turns 12CQ into licensable IP rather than a hardware competitor, and listed quantum names with no revenue and one credible physics claim have carried A$400m-1bn valuations this cycle. Biochip route: a CLIA-validated point-of-care potassium chip is a real medical-device business (dialysis, cardiology, emergency medicine) and such companies routinely reach A$300-600m with a cleared product and a partner. 100x = ~US$3.7bn is possible only if 12CQ becomes standard IP inside other people's machines - not underwritten, but not absurd from US$37m.

The mechanism is the memory wall: inference cost is dominated by moving weights and vectors, not arithmetic, and computing in-array removes the movement rather than accelerating it - largest advantage exactly for retrieval, similarity and vector search, now the default enterprise AI pattern. The legacy SRAM base is structurally shrinking and Q1 FY2027 revenue was already flat y/y. d-Matrix and EnCharge attack the same wall with far more capital, and further dilution is likely after the +31.9% share-count increase already absorbed.

IPWR.thesis: Ideal Power licenses B-TRAN, the only bidirectional bipolar transistor in existence: one device that conducts and blocks in both directions, halving conduction loss versus the back-to-back MOSFET/IGBT pairs every solid-state circuit breaker uses today. Nvidia's 800VDC Rubin Ultra rack architecture creates a socket that no incumbent device fills well, and a US hyperscaler is co-developing an 800V DC prototype for exactly that architecture. Market cap $63.9m at the 2026-09-16 close with $41.3m of cash and essentially no debt, so the market values the whole platform at roughly $22m.
IPWR.why_10x: 10x = $639m; since $41m of the $64m is cash, the operating business need only reach ~$598m. That requires one pathway - datacentre SSCB or EV contactor - to convert into a production design-in with device or royalty revenue in the tens of millions. An emerging power-semi platform with a named hyperscaler and a named auto OEM at $600m is unremarkable for the category. 100x = $6.4bn is arithmetically live (Navitas has traded near that on GaN) if B-TRAN becomes standard content in both DC datacentre protection and EV contactors; low probability, but the ~14-15 quarter runway is long enough to find out.
IPWR.what_kills_it: Pre-revenue for over a decade with a prior pivot (it was a solar inverter company) and $5,800 of quarterly revenue; hyperscaler co-development routinely ends without a purchase order and the partner is unnamed so nothing can be independently verified; Infineon/onsemi/Wolfspeed/Navitas can attack the same sockets with proven SiC and GaN at scale, and double-sided wafer processing is a real yield risk at volume.

limitations: Educational analysis. Not personalised investment advice. Nobody on this project is a licensed adviser, and every number below is a model output, not a forecast.

Estimation error dominates. The 5y sample means are extreme (several core lines annualise above 20%) because 2021-2026 contained a gold bull market, an AI capex boom and an oil spike. The 50/50 blend with CAPM halves that but does not remove it: the headline blended expected return of 15.4% for the core sits far above the CAPM-only estimate of 7.2%, and the truth is unlikely to be at the top of that range.

The optimiser is a maximiser of estimation error (Michaud 1989). Small changes in the expected-return vector move the weights a long way; the frontier and the four portfolios should be read as a map, not as a recommendation of one point on it.

The 12% volatility constraint binds on the ex-ante Ledoit-Wolf volatility of the optimised 97.5% of the core. Including the 2.5% SPCX policy weight at its 67-bar pairwise covariance raises the estimate to about 12.8%; SPCX's row and column of that matrix are not reliable.
SPCX has 67 daily bars. Its beta (2.95), volatility (90%) and every other statistic are reported for completeness and are not estimates.

No true 10-year backtest exists for this universe (see the log): the headline is 5 years of monthly rebalancing with no dealing costs, no 0.5%% stamp duty on the UK single stocks, no ~0.75%% ii FX charge on the non-GBP lines and no bid-offer spread. Real-world returns would be lower.
Backward-looking betas and correlations are computed against VWRP.L in GBP. ^FTAS stops on 2026-07-22 in Yahoo's feed, so the All-Share betas use a shorter sample.

The unicorn sleeve's 5y statistics are survivorship-biased: the 40 names were selected in 2026 from companies that still exist and still qualify. A sleeve chosen in 2021 on the same screen would contain names that have since failed.

The two individual gilts and the long-duration bond ETF get zero weight because the 50/50 blend averages a forward-looking redemption yield (T36N 5.30%, T56 5.87%) with a 5-year sample return of -4.0% and -11.1% a year -- the once-in-a-generation repricing from ~1% to ~5.3% yields that has ALREADY happened. For a gilt held to maturity the yield is the better estimate, and the expected_return_sensitivity block shows what the portfolio looks like when the optimiser is fed the yield/CAPM vector alone. This is a judgement call the Inputs tab should expose, not a settled answer.

Beta asymmetry is not robust: it changes sign with the measurement frequency AND with the treatment of SPCX. Measured on the optimised 97.5% alone (daily), the headline core has beta+ 0.66 below beta- 0.75, i.e. negative asymmetry; including the 2.5% SPCX policy weight at its own 67-bar betas -- the portfolio as actually held, and the convention the beta fields now use -- gives beta+ 0.85 against beta- 0.77, asymmetry +0.08. SPCX's 67-bar beta+ of 8.34 is not an estimate, so that positive figure rests on 67 days of one 2.5% line. On MONTHLY data the same weights give beta+ above beta- for the optimised part as well. Read the positive-skew claim as unproven either way rather than as established in either direction.

Concentration: SMGB.L (VanEck Semiconductor UCITS ETF) takes 16.6% of the headline core weight and contributes 35.8% of its ex-ante risk. The 20% single-ETF cap is what stops the largest ETF line going further; a tighter cap is a reasonable Inputs-tab experiment.
Reference portfolios are not constrained. EqualWeight breaches the 25% all-stocks cap (11 stocks x 2.71% = 29.6%) and is kept only as a comparison.
Listing-region weights record the LISTING VENUE, not economic exposure. Most core lines are LSE-listed UCITS wrappers holding global assets.
